target.title: fix: recover stranded replies in message_tool_only mode (#85714)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.visibleReplies` is set to `message_tool`, the agent is expected to call the message tool to deliver replies. If the LLM forgets (a probabilistic event — the reporter saw it happen on the 8th turn after 7 correct deliveries), the reply was **silently discarded**: the substantive text sat in the JSONL transcript but was never delivered to the user.

The existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal()` detection was already identifying these stranded replies and logging a warning, but took no recovery action.

## Fix

This commit promotes the detection from log-only to **followup retry**, preserving the `message_tool_only` privacy contract:

1. **Gate room events**: Skip stranded reply detection for ambient `room_event` turns where `message_tool_only` is automatically set by the system. Silence on room events is intentional by design — the agent chose not to respond.

2. **Enqueue followup retry turn**: When a stranded reply is detected, enqueue a followup run whose prompt instructs the agent to deliver the captured text via `message(action=send)`. The agent itself calls the message tool, so delivery happens through the correct contract path — no suppression bypass, no privacy boundary crossing.

3. **Clear transcript/persistence fields**: The retry run explicitly clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` from the original followup run to prevent the original user prompt from hiding the retry instruction. The followup runner resolves `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text`, so a retained `transcriptPrompt` would cause the agent to see the original user question instead of the retry delivery instruction.

4. **No suppression bypass**: This does NOT mark payloads with `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or use `skipSuppressionCheck`. The `message_tool_only` privacy contract is fully preserved: delivery only happens when the agent explicitly calls `message(action=send)`.

Normal (non-stranded) paths are unaffected: short replies, intentional `NO_REPLY`, and runs where the message tool already delivered are all excluded by the existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal` guard.

### Why followup retry instead of bypass delivery?

The `message_tool_only` contract says: "no message tool call = private/silent". Auto-publishing stranded text would break this documented behavior. Instead, we give the agent a second chance to follow the contract correctly — like returning an undelivered letter and asking the sender to mail it properly, rather than opening and publishing it ourselves.

## Changed files

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — followup retry with cleaned transcript fields, room_event gate (+26/-3 net)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — 5 new retry/gate tests replacing 6 bypass tests (-4 net)

## Tests

| Suite | Count | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| `agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` | 47 | ✅ All pass |
| `private-message-tool-final.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ All pass |
| `dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | 189 | ✅ All pass (unchanged, confirms no regressions) |
| `followup-runner.test.ts` | 67 | ✅ All pass (confirms followup queue compatibility) |

New test cases:
- `enqueues a followup retry for a stranded substantive reply (#85714)` — verifies `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with retry prompt containing the assistant text
- `does not enqueue retry for short private final replies` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry when the message tool delivered this turn` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry for room_event turns (#85714)` — verifies room_event gate
- `clears transcriptPrompt on retry to prevent original prompt from hiding retry instruction (#85714)` — regression test verifying `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` are all `undefined` on the retry run

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent's final message silently discarded when LLM forgets to call the message tool in `message_tool_only` mode. The fix enqueues a followup retry turn so the agent can deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, patched checkout at `9dc3c76dc3`.
- **Privacy contract preserved**: The fix does NOT use `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or `skipSuppressionCheck`. No payload is auto-delivered. The agent is re-prompted to call `message(action=send)` itself.
- **Transcript isolation**: The retry run clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` so the followup runner's `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text` resolution correctly uses the retry prompt, not the original user message.
- **Room event safety**: Stranded reply detection is gated by `sessionCtx.InboundEventKind !== "room_event"`, so ambient room events (where silence is intentional) never trigger recovery. Covered by dedicated test case.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, `warnPrivateMessageToolFinal` only logs — no retry is enqueued and the reply is silently lost.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  ✓ auto-reply agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts (47 tests) 1729ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  47 passed (47)

  ✓ unit-fast private-message-tool-final.test.ts (8 tests) 2ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)

  ✓ auto-reply dispatch-from-config.test.ts (189 tests) 3770ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  189 passed (189)

  ✓ auto-reply followup-runner.test.ts (67 tests) 1710ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  67 passed (67)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: When a stranded reply is detected, `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with a retry prompt containing the original assistant text and instructions to call `message(action=send)`. The retry run has `transcriptPrompt: undefined` so the followup runner correctly uses the retry instruction. Short replies, already-delivered replies, room events, and runs with existing transcript prompts are all verified by dedicated test cases.
- **What was not tested**: Live end-to-end delivery through an actual channel — the test verifies that the correct followup run is enqueued with the expected prompt shape and cleaned fields. The followup queue machinery (`enqueueFollowupRun` → `scheduleFollowupDrain` → `runReplyAgent`) is a well-tested existing mechanism used for concurrent message queuing.

## Real behavior proof (end-to-end, qa-lab host runner)

This adds a deterministic end-to-end proof that drives the real runtime loop — `runReplyAgent → stranded-final detection → warnPrivateMessageToolFinal → enqueueFollowupRun("stranded-reply-retry") → followup-runner → runEmbeddedAgent → message(action=send) → qa-channel outbound` — not the unit mocks (which stub `enqueueFollowupRun`/`runEmbeddedAgent`).

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Under `messages.visibleReplies=message_tool` (resolved `message_tool_only`), a substantive final reply that never calls the message tool was kept private and silently lost. The fix detects the stranded final and enqueues exactly one bounded followup retry that re-prompts the agent to deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract; if the retry strands again, no second retry is enqueued.
- **Real environment tested**: macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, branch `fix/stranded-reply-pending-delivery-85714` at current HEAD `0469009210` (rebased on latest upstream/main; recovery default-off + collect-batching isolation + updated scenario). qa-lab host runner: in-process gateway child + qa-channel bus + scenario-aware `mock-openai` provider (deterministic by construction; no live model, no Docker).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: ran the new scenario, PASS:
  ```
  node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite \
    --provider-mode mock-openai \
    --scenario message-tool-stranded-final-recovery \
    --concurrency 1 --fast
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: captured scenario result and the gateway's own runtime log line (ids redacted):
  ```
  COUNTS: { total: 1, passed: 1, failed: 0 }
  step: pass - recovered=1; stranded turns=1; retry delivery turns=1; WARN logged=true

  2026-06-06T06:31:23.411+08:00 [source-reply/private-final] agent produced a long private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool (message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered to the source channel
  ```
  Asserted from the live request/outbound capture:
  - Turn 1 request: `plannedToolName !== "message"` (long plain-text final, stranded).
  - Exactly one retry request plans the message tool, detected via the verbatim retry needle `you did not call message(action=send)`.
  - Retry delivery request: `plannedToolName === "message"`, `plannedToolArgs.action === "send"`, `plannedToolArgs.message === "QA-STRANDED-85714"`; one outbound on the direct conversation carried the marker (`recovered=1`).
  - After an 8s settle: outbound with the marker stays exactly 1 and message-tool retry deliveries stay exactly 1 (no loop).
- **Observed result after fix**: the stranded `message_tool_only` final was detected and warned, exactly one retry was enqueued, the retry delivered the original text via `message(action=send)` to the channel, and no second retry/delivery occurred — all four invariants observed against the real delivery path.
- **What was not tested**: not run against a live frontier model (deterministic mock by design, since a real model "forgetting" the tool is non-deterministic), and not on a real chat transport (Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord) — exercised on the in-process qa-channel bus; the `message(action=send)` → source-conversation outbound contract is transport-agnostic core auto-reply behavior.

target.title: fix(ios): reject loopback-prefix hosts for auth retry
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where iOS/shared Gateway auth retry could treat a remote hostname such as `127.attacker.example` as loopback during token-mismatch recovery. In that case, a stale shared gateway token plus a stored device token could cause the client to attempt device-token retry for a hostname that only looks loopback by prefix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retry trust gate now uses the existing structured loopback parser instead of a string prefix check, but keeps a retry-specific boundary that rejects unspecified bind hosts such as `0.0.0.0` and `::`. This keeps the auth-retry decision aligned with sibling retry behavior: real loopback endpoints remain eligible, prefix-bypass hostnames and wildcard bind addresses do not.

## User Impact

Users keep the intended local-device retry behavior for real loopback Gateway connections, while misleading remote hostnames and unspecified local bind addresses are no longer eligible for the more trusted device-token retry path. This is a narrow iOS/shared Gateway hardening fix with no new configuration or migration.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local --base origin/main` -> clean, no accepted/actionable findings
- Added focused Swift regression coverage for `ws://127.attacker.example:18789`, `ws://0.0.0.0:18789`, and `ws://[::]:18789`, verifying a second auth attempt keeps the shared token and does not attach the stored device token.
- GitHub CI on `92c27f3309524eb1006a8c2153cf17789aa15749`: `macos-swift`, `ios-build`, `Real behavior proof`, `security-fast`, and `preflight` passed.

target.title: [Bug]: Regression of #65533 — reasoning/reasoning_details completely dropped from message history for MiniMax M3 via OpenRouter (both plain-text and tool-call turns)
target.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

For MiniMax M3 via a custom OpenRouter provider, OpenClaw does not preserve `reasoning`/`reasoning_details` in message history for either plain-text or tool-call turns, despite OpenRouter returning this data in the same structure that worked correctly for MiniMax M2.x after #65533 was fixed — causing the model to fabricate a different answer than what it reasoned.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a custom OpenRouter provider in openclaw.json with model `openrouter/minimax/minimax-m3` with `thinkingDefault: "high"`
2. Enable I/O logging on the OpenRouter dashboard (Activity → View Logs) for the API key in use
3. Confirm thinking level is a non-off value
4. Plain-text test: send a multi-turn conversation where turn 1 asks the model to think of a random 8-digit number and hold it without saying it, then 2 filler turns, then ask it to reveal the number
5. Tool-call test: send "Search for the 3 files most recently modified in your workspace directory, then append those file names in a new `test.md` file in your workspace. Do it without saying anything until you're done!"
6. Inspect the Logs page for each test: compare the `reasoning`/`reasoning_details` fields present in each turn's response against their presence in the next request's message history

### Expected behavior

Per OpenRouter's documented `reasoning`/`reasoning_details` pass-back API (MiniMax M2 and newer explicitly supported), and consistent with the fix shipped (v2026.4.24) for #65533 (via `@mariozechner/pi-ai 0.70.2`), the `reasoning` string and/or `reasoning_details` array returned in a turn's response should be preserved on the corresponding assistant message when that turn is included in the history for the next request — for both plain-text and tool-call turns. A direct API call (bypassing OpenClaw) confirms M3 returns this data in the identical shape that worked for M2.x (see evidence).

With reasoning correctly preserved, the model should reveal the same number it reasoned about in turn 1.

### Actual behavior

In both test types, the assistant message for any prior turn appears in the next request's history with **no** `reasoning` or `reasoning_details` field, and no `<think>`-tag equivalent embedded in `content` either — the reasoning content is dropped entirely, not even concatenated (which was the behaviour of the original #65533 bug for plain-text turns).

**Plain-text test:** turn 1's reasoning contained the number `73184295`. By the final turn, the model answered "The number is 84736251" — a number that does not match its own original reasoning, demonstrating the model had no access to its prior thinking and fabricated a new answer.

**Tool-call test:** reasoning was present in every turn's response, but absent from every subsequent request's history — i.e., the tool-call path that was functioning fine pre and post #65533 is now also affected.

### OpenClaw version

2026.6.6

### Operating system

Ubuntu Server 24.04.4 LTS

### Install method

curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash

### Model

openrouter/minimax/minimax-m3

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> openrouter -> MiniMax

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence

**1. Final turn's request history — plain-text test (number test)**
The final request sent to OpenRouter, with turn 1's assistant message stripped of all reasoning:
```json
{
  "role": "user",
  "content": "Hey Tooru, could you help me out with a test? I'd like you to think of a random 8 digit number and memorise it, but don't say it out yet. I'll let you know when to tell me. I'm trying to debug the framework around this conversation so I need your help for this!"
},
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": "Got it! I've picked a random 8-digit number and I'm holding onto it. Just say the word and I'll share it. 🔢"
},
{
  "role": "user",
  "content": "Oh and, just to elaborate a bit more, it's actually about whether the framework (or agent harness rather) preserves all the text between turns. That's what this test is about. That's why it's important that you hold on to the number only in thought"
},
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": "Understood — got it. The number stays in my head only, not in any message text. Ready when you are. 🧠"
},
{
  "role": "user",
  "content": "Alright then! Let's try it. Tell me the number that you had originally thought up when I first asked!"
}
```
Turn 1's actual response (per OpenRouter parsed logs) contained:
```raw
Reasoning: "...I'll pick: 7,3,1,8,4,2,9,5 → 73184295..."
Completion: "Got it! I've picked a random 8-digit number and I'm holding onto it. Just say the word and I'll share it. 🔢"
```
No trace of this reasoning, in any form, appears in the final request's history.
**Resulting (incorrect) final output:**
```raw
The number is 84736251. 🔢
```
— which matches neither the original reasoning (73184295) nor any number in conversation text, confirming the model fabricated a new answer with no access to its original reasoning.

**2. Tool-call test**
Reasoning was present in every individual turn's response (confirmed via OpenRouter parsed logs), but absent from the messages array of every subsequent request — same pattern of complete loss, including for tool-call turns that worked correctly post (and pre) #65533.

**3. Raw OpenRouter API response for M3 (direct curl, bypassing OpenClaw)** — confirms OpenRouter returns reasoning for M3 in the same shape that worked for M2.x:
```json
"message": {
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": "Got it! I've thought of a random 8-digit number and I'll keep it hidden until you ask me to reveal it later. Just let me know when you're ready! 🔢",
  "refusal": null,
  "reasoning": "\nThe user is asking me to think of a random 8-digit number and hold onto it without revealing it yet. This is a simple request - they want me to generate a number and keep it secret for now. I should comply with this request.\n\nLet me think of a random 8-digit number. I could use a random number generator concept here, but since I'm an AI, I'll just pick one. Let me think of something truly random.\n\nLet me pick: 47298165\n\nThat's 8 digits. I'll hold onto this and not reveal it until they ask.\n",
  "reasoning_details": [
    {
      "type": "reasoning.text",
      "text": "\nThe user is asking me to think of a random 8-digit number and hold onto it without revealing it yet. This is a simple request - they want me to generate a number and keep it secret for now. I should comply with this request.\n\nLet me think of a random 8-digit number. I could use a random number generator concept here, but since I'm an AI, I'll just pick one. Let me think of something truly random.\n\nLet me pick: 47298165\n\nThat's 8 digits. I'll hold onto this and not reveal it until they ask.\n",
      "format": "unknown",
      "index": 0
    }
  ]
}
```
Both `reasoning` (string) and `reasoning_details` (array, `reasoning.text` type) are present — the same shape OpenClaw correctly consumed for MiniMax M2.x after the #65533 fix. This rules out an M3-specific response format change as the cause; the regression is in OpenClaw's history construction for M3.

### Impact and severity

- Affected users: Any OpenClaw user running MiniMax M3 via a custom OpenRouter provider with `reasoning: true` — for both conversational and agentic/tool-calling workflows
- Severity: Data integrity issue — the model produces confidently-stated answers that contradict its own prior reasoning, with no error surfaced to the user. For agentic tasks, this is the full loss of interleaved thinking that #65533 fixed
- Frequency: Always — observed consistently across both turn types in testing
- Consequence: Reasoning state is never carried forward for M3, regardless of turn type; user-visible incorrect outputs (e.g., the number mismatch) demonstrate this is not merely a performance degradation but produces directly wrong results

### Additional information

This appears related to #65533, but is a regression with broader impact: that issue was specifically about plain-text turns concatenating reasoning into `content`, while tool-call turns correctly used a separate `reasoning` field. In this case, for MiniMax M3, **both** turn types lose reasoning entirely — including the tool-call vs non-tool-call paths that was specifically the fix target of #65533. Combined with the confirmed-identical raw response shape (point 3 above), this suggests either a model-specific check in the converter that excludes M3 (e.g. a model-name allowlist that wasn't updated for M3), or a broader regression introduced since v2026.4.24 that re-broke both code paths.
Recommend referencing #65533 as a related/regressed issue rather than a duplicate, given the broader scope (tool-call path now also affected) and the new model (M3).

target.title: fix(ui): mobile-optimize gateway dashboard login gate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway Dashboard login gate (Control UI) is not mobile-optimized. On phones:

- Page (24px) + card (32px) padding eats ~112px of a 375px viewport, squeezing the form.
- The gate renders outside the app shell, so it gets no safe-area padding; with `viewport-fit=cover` the error card/help text runs into the iPhone home-bar area.
- Touch targets are below the 44px platform guideline: inputs ~35px, eye-toggle buttons 40px.
- The WebSocket URL field uses a default text keyboard with autocapitalize/autocorrect, which mangles `ws://` URLs, and it is the only field without Enter-to-connect.

## Why This Change Was Made

Users connect to the dashboard from phones (see screenshot workflow via `openclaw dashboard` QR/link). The login gate is the first surface they hit and should follow the mobile conventions the rest of the Control UI already uses (`layout.mobile.css` breakpoint, `--safe-area-*` vars, 44px targets).

## User Impact

On phones (≤768px, plus small-landscape):

- Tighter page/card padding with safe-area-aware insets — form gets usable width, nothing hides behind the home bar.
- 44px minimum touch targets for inputs, the token/password visibility toggles, and Connect.
- URL field: URL keyboard (`inputmode="url"`), no autocapitalize/autocorrect, "go" enter key, and Enter now connects (parity with token/password fields).
- Desktop rendering unchanged.

## Evidence

- Verified via Vite dev server with device emulation at 375×812 (portrait), 844×390 (landscape), and desktop width:
  - mobile: `.login-gate` padding `16px 12px` (safe-area `max()`), card `24px 20px`, computed `min-height: 44px` on inputs/Connect, 44×44 eye toggles.
  - desktop (>768px): unchanged `24px`/`32px` padding, no min-height overrides.
- Input font-size on real touch devices stays 16px (existing `(hover: none) and (pointer: coarse)` rule in `components.css`, which cascades after `layout.mobile.css`) — no iOS zoom-on-focus.
- `oxfmt --check` and `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` clean on both changed files.

target.title: fix(doctor): honor per-agent bootstrap profile in size check
target.body:
> AI-assisted: drafted with Claude Code. Bug discovery, fix, regression test, and behavior-proof reproducer all verified by the author on Windows 11 + Node 24.

## Summary

- Problem: `openclaw doctor` reports bootstrap-file-size warnings against the
  global `agents.defaults.bootstrap*MaxChars` budget even when the active
  default agent has a per-agent override under `agents.list[].bootstrap*MaxChars`,
  so the percentages, near-limit flags, and remediation tips are wrong for
  any setup that uses the per-agent profile feature added in #69966.
- Solution: thread the resolved `defaultAgentId` into the three call sites in
  `noteBootstrapFileSize` so the per-agent override is honored consistently
  with the rest of the runtime (`prepareCliRunContext`, `runEmbeddedAttempt`,
  `compactEmbeddedPiSessionDirectOnce`, and `/context` reporting), and update
  the remediation tip text to point at both the per-agent and defaults knobs.
- What changed: `src/commands/doctor-bootstrap-size.ts` resolves
  `defaultAgentId` once and passes it to `resolveBootstrapMaxChars`,
  `resolveBootstrapTotalMaxChars`, and `resolveBootstrapContextForRun`; the
  two truncation tips now mention `agents.list[].bootstrap*MaxChars` first
  with `agents.defaults.*` as fallback. `src/commands/doctor-bootstrap-size.test.ts`
  gains a regression test that asserts the agent id is threaded through, and
  the existing tip-text assertion is updated.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no behavior change for setups that
  rely solely on `agents.defaults.*` (the per-agent resolver falls back to
  defaults). No changes to budget math, warning thresholds, doctor command
  wiring, or other call sites (those were already correct after #69966).
  Doctor still inspects only the default agent's workspace; covering
  non-default agents is out of scope for this fix.

## Motivation

`feat(agents): support per-agent bootstrap profiles` (#69966, commit
`930852af29`) added `bootstrapMaxChars` / `bootstrapTotalMaxChars` /
`contextInjection` overrides under `agents.list[]` and threaded the resolved
session agent id through the embedded runner, CLI runner, compaction path,
and `/context` diagnostics. `noteBootstrapFileSize` in
`src/commands/doctor-bootstrap-size.ts` was missed in that thread-through, so
`openclaw doctor` still resolves only `agents.defaults.bootstrap*MaxChars`.

For users who configure a tighter or looser per-agent override, `openclaw
doctor` either over- or under-warns and the remediation tip points the user
at the wrong knob. The "Real behavior proof" section below shows three
scenarios producing identical wrong output on `origin/main` vs three
correctly differentiated outputs after this patch.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #69966 (introduced per-agent bootstrap profiles; this PR fills in
  the doctor call site missed by that thread-through)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: `openclaw doctor`'s `Bootstrap file size` note reports
percentages and remediation tips against `agents.defaults.bootstrap*MaxChars`
even when the default agent has a per-agent override set, so the reported
percent-of-max and tip wording do not match the budget the runtime actually
uses.

Real environment tested:
- OS: Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200
- Runtime: Node v24.14.1, pnpm 11.1.0 (corepack-pinned at `package.json`)
- Workspace: temp dir with a 25 000-char `AGENTS.md` to force truncation
- Config: default agent `main`, `agents.defaults.bootstrapMaxChars = 20 000`
  (`Total = 100 000`), `agents.list[main].bootstrapMaxChars` set per scenario

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```text
# Reproducer that imports noteBootstrapFileSize directly and captures stdout
# (the same code path openclaw doctor executes; the doctor command calls
# noteBootstrapFileSize from src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts:573).
# Running it against this branch yields the AFTER output below; checking out
# main first yields the BEFORE output (also captured below for comparison).
node --import tsx repro.local.mjs
```

Evidence after fix:

```text
=== A: defaults-only (defaultsMax=20000) ===

target.title: fix(gateway): run daily session resets on schedule
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users relying on configured daily session resets would see stale daily sessions persist past `atHour` until later inbound traffic touched the session-use reset path. During quiet periods, gateway uptime alone did not proactively roll those sessions over, so the configured daily reset contract was not enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

This branch moves daily reset evaluation into gateway maintenance, scans the configured session stores on a timer, and calls the existing reset service only for rows that are actually stale past the configured daily boundary. It intentionally preserves active runs and implicit provider-owned CLI sessions, and it reloads the current reset config on each sweep so policy changes take effect without a gateway restart.

## User Impact

Operators can now rely on daily session rollover happening during gateway uptime even when no new inbound message arrives after the reset boundary. Active runs stay bound, implicit provider-owned CLI sessions remain preserved under the default policy, and config changes to `session.reset`, `session.resetByType`, `session.resetByChannel`, or store targets are picked up on the next sweep.

## Evidence

Live source-checkout proof on the current branch exercised the real gateway maintenance timer against an isolated session store and showed the stale daily session rotating while the protected cases stayed intact:

- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout in a Linux container, on branch `fix-daily-session-reset`, running the patched gateway maintenance timer against an isolated temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. target.body:
Closes #99843

## What Problem This Solves

Long cached Anthropic tool loops could report aggregate cache billing buckets as
if they were one live context-window snapshot. That inflated token counts and
could trigger compaction well below the configured reserve threshold.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both Anthropic stream adapters now preserve the prompt snapshot from
`message_start` for context-window accounting while retaining the final
aggregate cache buckets for billing and cost reporting.

The shared context-token helper prefers an explicit prompt snapshot, then
derives the latest call's prompt size from `total - output`, and finally falls
back to component sums. Accumulated session usage remains component-based.
Metadata persistence and timeout-driven compaction use the same helper so the
decision is consistent across runner paths.

## User Impact

Cached Anthropic sessions no longer compact early because repeated cache-read
and cache-write billing totals are mistaken for the current prompt size.
Billing totals remain intact, and sessions above the real context threshold
still compact normally.

target.title: fix(openai): bound Codex image generation no-body response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a sibling OOM gap in OpenAI Codex OAuth image generation. The Codex Responses SSE path already bounds streamed bodies in `readResponseBodyText`, but the `!response.body` branch still called `response.text()` and only checked `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` after buffering the full payload. A faulty or hostile endpoint returning a body without a readable stream could still grow gateway memory without bound before the size guard fired.

## Why This Change Was Made

The no-body branch now fail-closes before any full-buffer fallback:

- reject oversized bodies from a trustworthy `Content-Length` header before calling `readResponseWithLimit` / `arrayBuffer()`
- reject missing or invalid `Content-Length` when no readable stream exists, instead of reading an unknown-size body
- only read bounded no-body payloads when `Content-Length` is present and within `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` (64 MiB)

This follows the same invariant as the existing streamed Codex image SSE guard:

- streamed Codex image SSE responses remain incrementally capped and cancelled on overflow

target.title: fix(runtime): guard JSON.stringify against circular tool output
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`writeRuntimeJson()`, the runtime `writeJson` method, and the plugin SDK `createLoggerBackedRuntime` all call `JSON.stringify(value)` on arbitrary tool return values. Circular references cause `TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON`, crashing the output path.

Improves on the contributor fix in #99490. The original fix used `String(value)` as the sole fallback, which ClawSweeper found can still throw for null-prototype circular objects (`Object.create(null)` with circular refs → `Cannot convert object to primitive value`).

## Root Cause

Three call sites in `src/runtime.ts` and `src/plugin-sdk/runtime-logger.ts` stringify unknown runtime values with unguarded `JSON.stringify(value, null, space)`:

| Call site | File | Line (HEAD) |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `createRuntimeIo().writeJson` | `src/runtime.ts` | 84 |
| `writeRuntimeJson` log fallback | `src/runtime.ts` | 116 |
| `createLoggerBackedRuntime().writeJson` | `src/plugin-sdk/runtime-logger.ts` | 31 |

`JSON.stringify` throws synchronously on circular structures, and there is no catch. The tool return value flows through these paths unchecked.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extracted a pure `safeJsonOutput(value, space?)` helper in `src/runtime.ts` that never throws:

1. `JSON.stringify(value)` — normal path
2. Catch → `JSON.stringify(String(value))` — handles ordinary circular refs
3. Catch → `"[unserializable]"` — last-resort for null-prototype objects where even `String()` throws

Key design decisions:
- **Serialization separated from I/O**: The helper returns a string; `writeStdout()` and `logger.info()` are called outside the try-catch. This preserves the existing EPIPE/EIO handling in `writeStdout`.
- **Shared across all call sites**: The plugin SDK `runtime-logger.ts` imports the same helper, so the three identical bug surfaces share one defensive path.
- **Nested try-catch, not replacer-based**: `JSON.stringify` replacer cannot intercept circular references (the engine throws before calling the replacer), so a catch-based fallback chain is the only reliable approach.

## Changes

- `src/runtime.ts`: +21/-9 lines
  - Added exported `safeJsonOutput(value, space?)` helper with nested try-catch
  - `createRuntimeIo().writeJson` → `writeStdout(safeJsonOutput(value, space))`
  - `writeRuntimeJson` log fallback → `runtime.log(safeJsonOutput(value, space))`
- `src/plugin-sdk/runtime-logger.ts`: +2/-1 lines
  - Import `safeJsonOutput`; `createLoggerBackedRuntime().writeJson` → `logger.info(safeJsonOutput(value, space))`
- `src/runtime.test.ts`: +48/-2 lines
  - 5 new `safeJsonOutput` unit tests + 6 `writeRuntimeJson` tests (rewritten)
- `src/plugin-sdk/runtime.test.ts`: +24 lines
  - 2 new tests for logger-backed runtime circular + null-prototype paths

## Evidence

### Verification environment

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| OS | Linux 4.19.112 x86_64 |
| Node.js | v22.19.0 |
| Vitest | v4.1.8 |

### Unit tests (15/15 passed, 7 new)

```
src/runtime.test.ts (11 tests)
 ✓ safeJsonOutput > serializes plain objects with default spacing
 ✓ safeJsonOutput > serializes compact without space
 ✓ safeJsonOutput > serializes with custom space
 ✓ safeJsonOutput > falls back to String(value) for circular references
 ✓ safeJsonOutput > falls back to constant for null-prototype circular references
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > serializes plain objects via writeJson
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > handles circular references via writeJson
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > handles null-prototype circular references via writeJson
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > delegates to runtime.log when writeStdout is absent
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > falls back to String(value) in log path for circular references
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > falls back to constant in log path for null-prototype circular references

src/plugin-sdk/runtime.test.ts (4 tests)
 ✓ resolveRuntimeEnv > returns provided runtime when present
 ✓ resolveRuntimeEnv > creates logger-backed runtime when runtime is missing
 ✓ resolveRuntimeEnv > handles circular references in logger-backed writeJson  ← NEW
 ✓ resolveRuntimeEnv > handles null-prototype circular in logger-backed writeJson  ← NEW
```

### Real-process proof: all 5 code paths (production code, no mocking)

Standalone script imports the production `safeJsonOutput`, `createNonExitingRuntime`, `writeRuntimeJson`, and `createLoggerBackedRuntime` via `tsx`. No mocking — real Node process running the actual production code paths.

```
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
OpenClaw Runtime JSON Guard — Real-Process Verification
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
PID:       <redacted>
Node:      v22.19.0
Platform:  linux x64

── Path A: safeJsonOutput (pure serializer) ──
  normal  : {"ok":true}
  circular: "[object Object]"
  null-ptr: "[unserializable]"
  Result:  PASS

── Path B: defaultRuntime (writeStdout path) ──
  normal  : {
  "status": "ok",
  "count": 3
}
  circular: "[object Object]"
  null-ptr: "[unserializable]"
  Result:  PASS

── Path C: writeRuntimeJson → writeJson (output delegation) ──
  circular → "[object Object]"
  null-ptr → "[unserializable]"
  Result:  PASS

── Path D: writeRuntimeJson → runtime.log (log fallback) ──
  normal  : { "key": "value" }
  circular → "[object Object]"
  null-ptr → "[unserializable]"
  Result:  PASS

── Path E: createLoggerBackedRuntime (plugin SDK logger) ──
  normal  : { "plugin": "test", "value": 42 }
  circular → "[object Object]"
  null-ptr → "[unserializable]"
  Result:  PASS

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VERDICT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  Normal objects serialized correctly                     PASS
  Circular refs → "[object Object]" (no crash)            PASS
  Null-proto circular → "[unserializable]" (no crash)     PASS
  writeStdout path handled                                PASS
  runtime.log fallback handled                            PASS
  Plugin SDK logger-backed runtime handled                PASS
  All 5 code paths exercised. No TypeError thrown.
```

### Comparison: PR #99490 vs this fix

| Scenario | `main` | #99490 `String(value)` | This PR |
|----------|--------|------------------------|---------|
| Normal `{ok: true}` | ✅ JSON | ✅ JSON | ✅ JSON |
| Circular `a.self = a` | ❌ TypeError | ✅ `"[object Object]"` | ✅ `"[object Object]"` |
| Null-proto circular | ❌ TypeError | ❌ TypeError | ✅ `"[unserializable]"` |
| Pipe error (EPIPE) | preserved | swallowed by catch | preserved |

## User Impact

- Prevents runtime crash when tools return objects with circular references
- The CLI outputs a safe fallback string instead of crashing
- Transparent to users; no config changes required
- Pipe-closed errors (EPIPE) continue to be handled correctly — the serialization catch does not interfere

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```

target.title: fix(google): bound embedding batch response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a sibling OOM risk to #98554 in Gemini/Google embedding batch handling. The Gemini batch upload/create error paths and completed output download path still had raw response body reads. A faulty or hostile Google-compatible endpoint could stream oversized error bodies, an oversized JSONL record, or extra/blank output records after a batch completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Google embedding batch code now uses the shared bounded provider HTTP readers for upload/create error bodies, and streams completed JSONL output one record at a time instead of buffering the whole file.

The output reader keeps valid large batch outputs working by allowing files larger than the provider text cap, while bounding the unsafe shapes:

- error response bodies are read with `readResponseTextLimited`
- each JSONL output record is capped at 4 MiB
- the number of output records is capped to the submitted request group size
- blank/whitespace JSONL records count against that record budget
- unknown `custom_id` rows are ignored instead of being stored in the result map

This follows the same invariant as the recent OpenAI embedding batch hardening: large valid JSONL output should stream successfully, but malformed single-record or unbounded provider output must be cancelled early.

## User Impact

Users running large Gemini embedding batches can still process valid large result files, and a bad provider response cannot grow gateway memory through unbounded response buffering or unlimited small output rows.

## Evidence

Loopback transport proof: I ran the production `runGeminiEmbeddingBatches` path against a local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1`. This uses the real `withRemoteHttpResponse` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` path, real HTTP `Response` streams, and no mocked `fetch`.

target.title: fix(discord): fall back to text when voice delivery fails
target.body:
## Summary

This fixes a Discord final-reply failure mode I hit locally: when an `audioAsVoice` reply failed during voice-note delivery, the reply could disappear completely instead of falling back to visible text.

- Try Discord voice-note delivery first, as before.
- If voice delivery fails and there is visible text, send that text instead.
- If the visible text was stripped into a hidden TTS supplement, use that supplement text as the fallback.
- Keep the change scoped to the Discord payload path; direct media sending and unrelated voice behavior are intentionally out of scope.

Success here is pretty simple: if Discord voice delivery fails, the user still gets the answer as text.

Reviewers should focus on the `audioAsVoice` payload ordering and fallback behavior, especially reply targets, TTS supplement handling, and avoiding duplicate text after an already-delivered supplement.

## Linked context

Closes: N/A

Related: #84952, #85173

This came from a real local OpenClaw Discord setup where a final reply tried to go out as a voice note and failed before any visible reply was sent.

Issue #84952 / PR #85173 are in the same Discord `audioAsVoice` fallback area, but they cover a different failure mode: voice adapter unavailable in cron/text-only delivery, with fallback to text+media attachment. This PR covers the final payload path where voice delivery is attempted and then rejects; the intended fallback here is visible text, including hidden TTS supplement text when that is the only available transcript.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Discord `audioAsVoice` final replies could fail the voice path and send no text fallback.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout on this branch, using a real Discord bot/account and a private Discord test channel.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran the patched `sendDiscordOutboundPayload` path directly with `audioAsVoice: true`, visible fallback text, and deliberately invalid audio input so the voice conversion path failed.
- Evidence after fix:

```json
{
  "voiceAttempted": true,
  "voiceFailure": "Command failed: /usr/bin/ffmpeg -y -i /tmp/openclaw/voice-src-mMImTx/input.html ...",
  "result": {
    "messageId": "1511791135129997482",
    "channelId": "1510545702881595392",
    "channel": "discord"
  },
  "fetchedStatus": 200,
  "fetchedMessage": {
    "content": "OpenClaw PR proof 2026-06-03T17:58:13.575Z: voice delivery failed on purpose, text fallback worked.",
    "attachmentCount": 0,
    "type": 0
  }
}
```

- Observed result after fix: voice delivery was attempted, ffmpeg failed during conversion, and the fallback text was still posted to Discord. Fetching the message back from Discord showed matching text and `attachmentCount: 0`, so it was a text fallback rather than a voice attachment.
- What was not tested: I did not run a full end-to-end gateway deployment with `/usr/bin/ffmpeg` removed from the host.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: the original local failure involved ffmpeg not being available to the runtime. I could not safely rename `/usr/bin/ffmpeg` in this environment because non-interactive sudo is not available, so the live proof forces a realistic voice-delivery failure by giving ffmpeg invalid audio input instead. That still exercises the patched failure boundary: `sendVoice` rejects, then the payload path sends text.
- Before evidence: before this change, the `audioAsVoice` branch awaited voice delivery directly. If that threw, the payload send failed before visible text or hidden TTS supplement text could be sent.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

- `CI=true pnpm test extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.extensions.json --noEmit`
- `pnpm test:extension discord`
- `codex review --base origin/main`

Regression coverage added/updated:

- falls back to visible text when Discord voice delivery rejects
- falls back to hidden TTS supplement text when visible text was stripped for voice delivery
- preserves the reply target when falling back from voice to text
- suppresses duplicate TTS supplement text when it was already visibly delivered

What failed before this fix: a rejected Discord voice send in the final payload path could prevent any text reply from being delivered.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? `Yes`

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? `No`

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? `No`

Highest-risk area: the ordering around Discord `audioAsVoice` payloads, because voice notes cannot include text, while fallback text still needs to preserve reply threading and avoid duplicates.

How that risk is mitigated: the change is limited to the Discord payload send path, keeps successful voice delivery behavior first, and adds focused regression coverage for the fallback cases and duplicate-suppression case.

## Current review state

Next action: maintainer review.

Still waiting on: upstream CI and any maintainer preference on wording or fallback policy.

Bot/reviewer comments addressed: `codex review --base origin/main` came back clean with no findings after the latest branch state.

target.title: fix(slack): reconcile ambiguous sends before replay
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack can commit a final message while the local sender loses the response. Recovery previously had no exact provider-side proof for that ambiguous outcome, so replay could duplicate the final answer or conservative recovery could strand the queue entry.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Attach an opaque authenticated delivery marker to every Slack text chunk. The signature binds the durable queue id, concrete Slack channel, thread target, chunk index, and chunk count.
- Persist the canonical post-hook reply target and the final pre-API dispatch time in the durable queue, then reconcile only inside a bounded attempt window.
- Require the complete authenticated chunk set before acknowledging a recovered send. Missing markers remain unresolved because Slack does not expose a supported caller-supplied idempotency key for `chat.postMessage`.
- Keep exact reconciliation opt-in. Ordinary lower-level required queue sends, media, blocks, and payload transports retain their existing behavior.
- Try both configured read and write token views when visibility differs, while preserving conflict/incomplete evidence.

## User Impact

Ambiguous Slack final text sends can now be proven from Slack history and acknowledged without posting a duplicate. Thread replies, user-targeted DMs, message chunking, multiple Slack token views, hook-adjusted reply targets, and recovery restarts retain the exact route needed for reconciliation.

## Evidence

- Live Slack proof: posted a three-part top-level message and a threaded reply through the rewritten send path; both reconciled the exact authenticated metadata set, dispatch persistence ran once per logical send immediately before posting, and every temporary message was deleted.
- Slack extension suite: 106 files, 1,459 tests passed.
- Focused core/Slack regression set: queue storage/recovery, message orchestration, inbound durable delivery, CLI bridge, and Slack adapter/reconciliation tests passed.

target.title: feat(workboard): expose dispatch --max-starts to raise the per-pass start cap
target.body:
Closes #100169

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where operators running `openclaw workboard dispatch` (or calling the `workboard.cards.dispatch` Gateway RPC) could not raise the number of new worker runs started per dispatch pass. The dispatcher hard-caps new starts at **3 per pass**, and there was no CLI flag or RPC parameter to change it — the only workaround was patching the installed plugin bundle. On a board with sustained ready volume, throughput was pinned far below what the host could support.

Internally, `dispatchAndStartWorkboardCards` already accepted `options.maxStarts`, but nothing above it populated the value: the CLI `dispatch` command exposed only `--board`/`--json`, and the Gateway handler read only `boardId` off the request.

## Why This Change Was Made

Thread `maxStarts` end to end so the existing internal option is reachable by operators:

- **CLI** (`extensions/workboard/src/cli.ts`): add `--max-starts <count>` (validated as a positive integer) to the `dispatch` command and forward it in the Gateway params, but only when the flag is supplied.
- **Gateway** (`extensions/workboard/src/gateway.ts`): read `maxStarts` off the incoming request params and pass it into `dispatchAndStartWorkboardCards`, preserving the built-in default of `3` when the param is absent.

Scope is deliberately narrow. The default cap and the one-card-per-owner selection rule are unchanged, so behavior is identical when the flag/param is omitted. **Persistent config and parallelizing the currently-sequential start loop are intentionally left out** — the issue triage flagged both as needing a maintainer product/resource-policy decision first (new plugin config surface; changed host/subagent concurrency semantics). This PR ships only the "narrowest safe first step" that triage endorsed.

## User Impact

Operators can now tune dispatch throughput per pass:

```bash
openclaw workboard dispatch --max-starts 10
```

With no flag, nothing changes — dispatch still starts at most 3 workers per pass. The one-card-per-owner rule still applies, so the effective number of starts can be lower than the cap. Non-positive values are rejected with a clear error.

## Evidence

Focused tests added (CI will run them):

- `extensions/workboard/src/cli.test.ts`
  - forwards `--max-starts` into the `workboard.cards.dispatch` params
  - omits `maxStarts` from the params when the flag is absent
  - rejects a non-positive `--max-starts` value
- `extensions/workboard/src/gateway.test.ts`
  - threads `maxStarts` from Gateway request params into dispatch (two eligible cards under distinct owners, `maxStarts: 1` starts exactly one)

Docs updated in `docs/cli/workboard.md` (synopsis, example, and the dispatch-selection notes).

> Note: I could not run the suite locally — this monorepo requires `pnpm@11` and Node `>=22.19` (the local toolchain had neither), so validation is left to CI.


---

## Behavior proof (after fix)

Deterministic terminal output exercising the **exact `--max-starts` parser from this PR** (`extensions/workboard/src/cli.ts`), old vs new, across representative inputs. It shows the strict-decimal change rejecting notation that `Number()` silently coerced:

```text
workboard --max-starts parsing (old Number() vs new strict decimal)

input      old Number()   new strict
"7"        7              7        
"10"       10             10       
"0"        REJECTED       REJECTED 
"1e3"      1000           REJECTED   <-- coercion fixed
"0x10"     16             REJECTED   <-- coercion fixed
"5.5"      REJECTED       REJECTED 
" 4 "      4              4        
"-2"       REJECTED       REJECTED 
"abc"      REJECTED       REJECTED 
```

`1e3` and `0x10` previously parsed to 1000 / 16; they are now rejected, while plain decimals still work. The `maxStarts` threading itself (CLI flag → gateway params → dispatcher cap) is covered by the focused tests in `cli.test.ts` / `gateway.test.ts`, which CI runs against the real modules.

target.title: feat(feishu): configure card footer

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu agent replies already render structured cards with a gray note footer, but operators cannot customize that footer from config. This makes the main agent card footer fixed to the generated `Agent / Model / Provider` metadata instead of allowing a deployment-specific label or operational note.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a Feishu plugin `cardFooter` config field and wires it into the existing structured-card note rendering path instead of adding a new card layout. The setting is shared config, so it works at `channels.feishu.cardFooter` and can be overridden per account with `channels.feishu.accounts.<id>.cardFooter`.

When unset or blank, Feishu cards keep the current generated footer. That preserves existing behavior while giving operators a small, explicit customization hook for main agent cards and other agent reply cards.

## User Impact

Users can configure a custom footer note for Feishu/Lark agent cards. The value is used on both streaming cards and complete structured-card replies. Existing configs continue to show the current generated `Agent: ... | Model: ... | Provider: ...` footer when `cardFooter` is not set.

target.title: fix(macos): prevent hatch and web chat from timing out on slow first replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS onboarding/web chat could make a slow first assistant reply look stuck or prematurely timed out when the selected model takes longer than the old client-side budget. This matters for first-run hatch/chat paths with slower models such as OpenAI 5.5, where the user expects the assistant to keep working after they describe its purpose.

The mismatch was that the macOS WebChat path needed a longer assistant-run budget and a completion observation path, while the request/ACK deadline should still fail quickly when the gateway is unreachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

This separates the short request/ACK deadline from the actual WebChat assistant run budget. The shared `GatewayConnection.chatSend` default stays request-sized so other macOS callers such as Talk Mode keep their existing timeout policy, while `MacGatewayChatTransport.sendMessage` explicitly opts WebChat/hatch into a five-minute `timeoutMs` run budget.

The shared chat UI now reads its pending/completion budget from the transport: default transports keep a 30-second pending wait, and macOS WebChat explicitly opts into the five-minute window through `MacGatewayChatTransport.pendingRunTimeoutMs`. macOS WebChat also waits for completion through existing Gateway `agent.wait` before refreshing history. The change uses existing Gateway surfaces (`chat.send.timeoutMs` and `agent.wait`) and does not change gateway protocol shape, auth, provider routing, model selection, session storage, schema, migrations, iOS transport behavior, or delivery channels.

## User Impact

macOS users hatching or chatting with a newly configured assistant now get a realistic wait window and a production completion observation path for slow first replies instead of a premature timeout or stuck-looking state while the assistant run may still be active or recently completed.

The intended behavior is that macOS WebChat/hatch keeps gateway ACK failures prompt while giving only the WebChat assistant run, UI pending state, and completion refresh path the first-run-sized five-minute window. Shared/default chat transports keep the existing 30-second pending budget unless they explicitly opt into a longer one.

## Evidence

Native macOS visual/accessibility proof on the PR build, using the native `OpenClaw Chat` window and a session-level `openai/gpt-5.3-codex-spark` override for this proof run:

```

    AXStaticText value='Gateway connected'
```

After the slow run completed, the same native window cleared the pending state and showed the final assistant reply:

```text

AXWindow name='OpenClaw Chat' desc='standard window'

    AXScrollArea
      AXOpaqueProviderGroup desc='list'
        AXStaticText value='For local PR #97722 native WebChat visual proof only: use the shell tool to run exactly sleep 45 with no output, then reply exactly native WebChat slow reply proof complete.'

Post-scope validation for this follow-up commit:

target.title: [codex] active-memory default to configured agents
target.body:
## Summary

- Default Active Memory to configured OpenClaw agents when `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents` is omitted.
- Fall back to the implicit `main` agent for minimal configs that do not define `agents.list`.
- Preserve explicit empty `config.agents: []` as no targeted agents.
- Preserve explicit non-empty `config.agents` allowlist behavior.
- Document the targeting contract in the Active Memory docs and plugin config help.

This matters because omitting `config.agents` previously normalized to an empty list, so Active Memory was disabled for every agent. The intended outcome is that operators can enable Active Memory across configured agents without maintaining a duplicated allowlist, while minimal single-agent configs still target `main`.

Out of scope: changing chat type filtering, per-session toggles, memory indexing behavior, or the memory tools used by the Active Memory sub-agent.

Review focus: whether the fallback to `agents.list[].id`, then implicit `main`, is the right default, and whether explicit empty/non-empty `config.agents` remains unchanged.

## Linked context

Closes #

Related #82528

This came from running OpenClaw with multiple Telegram topics routed to separate agents and needing Active Memory to apply consistently without copying the same agent list into plugin config.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior addressed:
  Omitting `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents` normalized to an empty allowlist, so Active Memory skipped every agent instead of applying to configured agents.
- Real environment tested:
  OpenClaw 2026.6.5 on a Linux host with a systemd user gateway, Telegram group topics routed to `main`, `sementes`, `cloudfarm`, and `pedro-agenda`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  Applied the equivalent runtime change locally, removed `active-memory.config.agents`, restarted `openclaw-gateway`, then checked gateway status and memory search.
- Evidence after fix:

```text
openclaw gateway status --deep
Gateway version: 2026.6.5
Runtime: running
Capability: admin-capable
```

```text
journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway --since "3 minutes ago"
[gateway] http server listening (12 plugins: active-memory, brave, browser, canvas, codex, device-pair, file-transfer, memory-core, openai, phone-control, talk-voice, telegram; 12.1s)
```

```text
openclaw memory search --query "Pedro SeedSearch Markus" --max-results 5
0.545 memory/pendencias-grupo.md:1-21
0.516 memory/2026-03-31.md:1-37
0.453 memory/dreaming/light/2026-06-05.md:43-72
```

- Observed result after fix:
  Active Memory no longer required a hardcoded `config.agents` list to apply across configured agents.
- What was not tested:
  A fresh live Telegram command round-trip was not captured on the final PR branch.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints:
  The production server was restored to upstream behavior after proof collection, using an explicit `config.agents` list until this PR is merged upstream.
- Before evidence:
  Reading the prior plugin implementation showed `normalizePluginConfig({}).agents` became `[]`, while `isEnabledForAgent` requires `config.agents.includes(agentId)`.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
pnpm docs:list
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/active-memory/index.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts docs/concepts/active-memory.md extensions/active-memory/openclaw.plugin.json
pnpm exec oxlint extensions/active-memory/index.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts
node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/concepts/active-memory.md
node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check
node --import tsx -e "import { testing } from './extensions/active-memory/index.ts'; const cfg={agents:{list:[{id:'main'},{id:'support'}]}}; console.log(JSON.stringify({ omitted: testing.normalizePluginConfig({}, cfg).agents, empty: testing.normalizePluginConfig({agents: []}, cfg).agents, explicit: testing.normalizePluginConfig({agents:['support']}, cfg).agents, implicitMain: testing.normalizePluginConfig({}).agents }, null, 2));"
git diff --check upstream/main -- docs/concepts/active-memory.md extensions/active-memory/index.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts extensions/active-memory/openclaw.plugin.json
.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD
```

Regression coverage added:

- `defaults to all configured agents when no active-memory agent allowlist is set`
- `preserves an empty active-memory agent allowlist`
- `defaults to the implicit main agent when no agent list is configured`
- `keeps an explicit active-memory agent allowlist`

CI after the latest push:

- Pending for commit `b7e75ed8eaa7`. Prior CI was green on `fdf408d1e55464aced878f0fee85201324590de3`.

Final-head normalization proof on `b7e75ed8eaa7`:

```json
{
  "omitted": [
    "main",
    "support"
  ],
  "empty": [],
  "explicit": [
    "support"
  ],
  "implicitMain": [
    "main"

}
```

Autoreview note:

- The final commit review still flags the omitted-`agents` default as a maintainer compatibility decision. That is the intended product change in this PR and remains called out below; the explicit empty-list finding has been addressed.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes`)

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes`)

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`No`)

Highest-risk area:
Operators who intentionally omitted `config.agents` expecting Active Memory to run nowhere would now get Active Memory for configured agents, or `main` in minimal configs. Explicit `config.agents: []` continues to target no agents.

Risk mitigation:
Explicit `config.agents: []` remains a no-target allowlist, and explicit non-empty `config.agents` still behaves as an allowlist. Operators can set `enabled: false`, disable the plugin entry, set `agents: []`, or provide a narrow `agents` list when they want less coverage. The docs and manifest help now state the omitted default and the explicit-empty behavior.

## Current review state

Next action:
Await maintainer compatibility decision for omitted `config.agents` and CI completion on the latest commit.

GitHub PR checks for the latest push and maintainer decision on the omitted-agent default policy.

Bot/reviewer comments addressed:

target.title: fix(active-memory): keep recall circuit breaker tripped across cooldown
target.body:
Closes #100167 ## What Problem This Solves Resolves a problem where agents with the `active-memory` plugin enabled pay a fixed recall-timeout stall (~15s by default) on **every** turn once recall starts failing, instead of the plugin backing off. The reporter saw `status=timeout summaryChars=0` on every `main`-agent turn for 24+ hours, making latency-sensitive flows (Talk / live voice, direct chat) feel unresponsive. The plugin already has a circuit breaker (#74054) that is supposed to skip recall after `circuitBreakerMaxTimeouts` consecutive timeouts. But on cooldown expiry it **deleted the failure record entirely**. At normal turn cadence — turns spaced further apart than `circuitBreakerCooldownMs` (default 60s, max 10m) — the consecutive-timeout count reset to zero before it could ever reach the threshold, so the breaker never re-engaged and every turn ran the sub-agent into the watchdog again. ## Why This Change Was Made Make the breaker **half-open** across the cooldown instead of resetting ([`extensions/active-memory/index.ts`](extensions/active-memory/index.ts)): - After the cooldown, allow a single **probe** recall through but keep the tripped record. A probe timeout re-opens the breaker immediately (one recorded timeout, not `maxTimeouts` fresh ones); a successful recall clears it via the existing `resetCircuitBreaker` path. - Track the in-flight probe so only one runs at a time, and **self-heal**: if a probe is lost (aborted without recording a timeout or success), another is allowed once a full cooldown has elapsed — the breaker can never stick permanently open and silently disable recall. ## User Impact A persistently failing agent/model now pays the recall timeout **at most once per cooldown window** instead of on every turn. Recovery is unchanged — the next successful recall clears the breaker. Existing config (`circuitBreakerMaxTimeouts`, `circuitBreakerCooldownMs`) is unchanged; docs updated to describe the half-open behavior. ## Scope / Honest Limitations This is deliberately scoped to the **recurring per-turn timeout tax**, which is the measurable user impact. It does **not** change *why* the embedded recall run produces zero model output (`payloads=0`, `stopReason=missing`) on the reporter's specific stack (openai `gpt-5.5` + codex app-server + `lossless-claw` per-turn projection). Notably, the issue's suggested root cause (empty prompt from `assembledMessages: 0`) does not hold up in code: [`context-engine-projection.ts`](extensions/codex/src/app-server/context-engine-projection.ts) falls back to the raw recall prompt as `promptText` when there is no assembled context, and that text is sent to Codex — so the prompt is not empty. Pinning down the real zero-output cause needs a live repro on that provider stack, which is why triage labeled the issue `needs-live-repro`. That part is left for a follow-up with live evidence. One known limitation of this fix: turns spaced further apart than the maximum cooldown (10m) still probe on each turn by design; operators on very low-cadence chats can raise `circuitBreakerCooldownMs` to widen protection. ## Evidence Focused unit tests added in [`extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts`](extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts): - After the cooldown, one probe is allowed through, the tripped record is retained (not deleted), and a **single** probe timeout re-opens the breaker immediately — the exact regression behind #100167. - A lost half-open probe lets another probe through after a further cooldown (no permanent stick), and a successful recall clears the breaker. Existing breaker tests (skip-within-cooldown, `circuit breaker open` log, reset-on-success) remain valid under the new behavior. > Note: I could not run the suite locally — this monorepo requires `pnpm@11` and Node `>=22.19` (not available in my environment), so CI runs the tests. --- ## Behavior proof (after fix) Real capture from the openai/`gpt-5.5` + codex app-server + `lossless-claw` stack isn't available to me (that's the `needs-live-repro` gate). But this fix is a state-machine change, so here is deterministic terminal output that exercises the **exact breaker logic from this PR** (old vs new functions, virtual clock) against a recall that always times out — i.e. the condition reported in #100167 where every turn logs `status=timeout summaryChars=0`: ```text active-memory recall breaker — recall always times out (as in #100167) config: maxTimeouts=3 cooldown=60s timeout=15s == Talk / live-voice cadence (30 turns, 3s apart) == OLD: ran=6/30 dead-time=90s RUN RUN RUN skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip RUN RUN RUN skip skip skip skip skip NEW: ran=4/30 dead-time=60s RUN RUN RUN skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip RUN skip skip skip skip skip skip skip == Direct chat, brisk cadence (20 turns, 20s apart) == OLD: ran=12/20 dead-time=180s RUN RUN RUN skip skip RUN RUN RUN skip skip RUN RUN RUN skip skip RUN RUN RUN skip skip NEW: ran=8/20 dead-time=120s RUN RUN RUN skip skip RUN skip skip RUN skip skip RUN skip skip RUN skip skip RUN skip skip == Sparse cadence (turns > cooldown apart) (8 turns, 3600s apart) == OLD: ran=8/8 dead-time=120s RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN NEW: ran=8/8 dead-time=120s RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN ``` Reading it: - **Brisk direct chat** is the clearest: OLD re-runs **3** recalls every cooldown cycle (`RUN RUN RUN skip skip …`, 180s dead-time), NEW re-runs only **1** (`RUN skip skip …`, 120s) because the tripped record is retained instead of deleted. - **Talk / live-voice** cadence: OLD 6 runs, NEW 4 — and NEW stays skipped far longer after tripping. - **Sparse cadence** (turns further apart than the cooldown): OLD == NEW, both probe every turn. This is the documented limitation — the fix caps repeated timeouts within a cooldown window, it can't help traffic slower than the cooldown. Operators raise `circuitBreakerCooldownMs` for that.
Reproduce (plain node, no deps) The script mirrors `isCircuitBreakerOpen` / `recordCircuitBreakerTimeout` from `extensions/active-memory/index.ts` verbatim and simulates turn sequences. The same logic is covered by the unit tests in `extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts`, which CI runs against the real module.
